key_insight: The paper shows that neutrino oscillations can be efficiently simulated on superconducting hardware by encoding the neutrino states in a cavity’s bosonic Fock modes and controlling them with a single ancilla qubit.
engineering_relevance: This demonstrates a hardware-friendly alternative to qubit-only encodings for quantum simulation, leveraging SNAP and displacement pulses for high-fidelity cavity control.
method: Encode two- and three-flavor neutrino states in the Fock basis of a microwave cavity mode
Implement the required unitaries with selective number-dependent arbitrary phase (SNAP) and displacement gates
Use pulse-level control with a single ancillary qubit to drive and read out the bosonic simulation
evidence_signal: The simulated neutrino oscillation probabilities closely match theoretical predictions, indicating successful gate implementation and model fidelity.
watch_item: The approach relies on precise pulse calibration and cavity control, so scaling and sensitivity to hardware errors may limit practical deployment.
paper_title: Quantum simulation of neutrino oscillations with bosonic encoding
